what: 63 trap locations exist only as a map (S1 Fig) and a text count by state. The format has no typed location (coordinates, area, reference system), so the study's spatial coverage cannot be searched or compared with other insect studies.
Trap permits went into `ethics` as an approval: they are not ethics reviews. No place for collection permits.

Sampling effort (16,908 exposure days, emptying interval 11.2 ± 6.3 days), trap design and the location-year structure (37/20/5/1 locations sampled in 1/2/3/4 years) have no fields; they live in text.
Biomass is of all insects, unidentified. Studies that identify taxa (GBIF/NCBITaxon) would need taxa as definitions: kind `population`? `other`? There is no kind for organisms or taxa.
6.1% annual decline is reported with a coefficient's SD (sd = 0.002), not an interval. SD/SE of an estimate cannot be typed; I dropped it.

Model comparison (DIC, pD, R2 per model) fits a table well; the 'trend survives covariates' claim reads off it. No friction beyond Bayesian credible intervals being stored as `interval` with level 0.95 and no way to say 'credible'.
The key unstated assumption (trap catch represents local biomass; trap attractiveness constant over 27 years) is mine, provenance `inferred`. Fine.
